scope: Targeted independent clinical audit; 12 clinical evidence units plus guideline, HTA and product-label records. Not a systematic review, regulatory opinion, clinical recommendation or investment guarantee.

findings.claim: Nifedipine has credible independent clinical activity; the extra benefit from adding lidocaine to nifedipine remains unresolved.
No same-strength randomized chronic-fissure comparison of nifedipine/lidocaine versus nifedipine alone was retrieved in this targeted search.
findings.status: search finding, not proof of absence

findings.claim: Short-term healing, pain relief, recurrence and investor cash recovery are separate outcomes.
P001/98 in the Canadian label and the Perrotti2002 report apparently share an evidence lineage; the day21/day42 and healing-definition differences need reconciliation.
Existing repeated-dose healthy-volunteer and single-dose injured-mucosa PK precede this proposal. A new PK study must answer an identified remaining question.

confidence.question: Nifedipine can help short-term fissure healing
confidence.basis: Multiple controlled studies, differing articles and populations; small studies and reporting/attrition weaknesses.

confidence.question: Fixed 0.3%/1.5% combination adds clinically useful benefit over nifedipine alone
confidence.basis: No direct component-removal comparison retrieved; much evidence adds nifedipine to lidocaine.

confidence.question: Durable healing after stopping treatment
confidence.basis: Heterogeneous recurrence reports, endpoints and follow-up; no pooled estimate.

confidence.question: Broad absence of systemic exposure or adverse effects
confidence.basis: Lidocaine measurable after surgery; small samples cannot exclude uncommon events.

confidence.question: High-probability investor capital recovery
confidence.basis: Requires product differentiation, attainable economics, territory and regulatory route.

next_milestone.status: proposed, no outreach or expenditure authorized here
next_milestone.class: Clinical evidence and exact-product decision package before new human exposure
next_milestone.deliverable: One reconciled evidence map and go/no-go comparison for an existing 0.3%/1.5% article, a changed formulation/delivery article, and nifedipine alone.
priority_checks: Reconcile P001/98 protocol/CSR, day21 versus day42, complete versus almost-complete healing, analysis population and prespecified pain endpoints.
Map the proposed article against each study: strength, vehicle, administration site, dose delivery, stability, exposure and clinical claim.
Assess whether lidocaine adds a material product benefit that requires direct evidence; do not infer this from trials in which both arms contain lidocaine.
Separate the full source-data access/right-to-reference question from the scientific plausibility of the published results.
Determine the specific target-jurisdiction evidentiary gap using existing public labels and assessments before selecting an experiment.
sequence_if_gaps_remain: For an unchanged transferable article, audit the existing dossier and manufacturing comparability before commissioning generic PK.
For a changed vehicle or applicator, begin with comparative pharmaceutical performance and delivered-dose feasibility; these tests cannot establish clinical equivalence by themselves.
For an unresolved exposure difference, define a focused exposure bridge; healthy repeated-dose data do not settle repeated exposure on damaged mucosa.
For a claim that lidocaine adds benefit, a component-comparison clinical study may be needed, but only after the regulatory and commercial claim is chosen.
For an independent new efficacy claim, design the clinical program around the required pain/healing endpoint and meaningful follow-up; a small uncontrolled series would add little.
next_milestone.estimate_basis: Subjective desk-work duration for a focused clinical/regulatory/product gap package, excluding unavailable sponsor data, experiments, ethics review and regulator waiting time. Not a quote or approval timetable.
stop_or_redirect_conditions: The apparent opportunity requires repeating already available PK without resolving a valuable product or regulatory gap.
The chosen claim requires a substantially larger clinical program than the contemplated bounded bridge.
The combination adds no defendable patient/product benefit and a simpler article has superior obtainable economics.
The exact article or needed source-data reliance cannot be obtained on acceptable terms after later commercial diligence.

sources.access: Guideline recommendations only; not counted as a new clinical cohort.

sources.title: HAS NIFEXINE assessment: pain associated with chronic anal fissure
sources.access: Official HTA summary. Cited for HAS's judgment; not independent efficacy evidence or a US regulatory requirement.

limitations: Acute disease and different strength; not exact-product chronic replication.
Comparator changes both nifedipine and hydrocortisone/lidocaine exposure.

evidence_units.design: Randomized double-blind; single center per HAS
limitations: Lidocaine present in both arms; cannot estimate its added benefit.
Steroid comparator is not inert; its causal contribution to the low control healing is unproven.
Same apparent cohort as P001/98; reconcile endpoint timing/definition with CL15.

arms.article: Topical glyceryl trinitrate; concentration unverified here

limitations: Small study; recurrence denominators not explicit in retrieved abstract.
Six-month healing window differs from short fixed-time outcomes.

evidence_units.exposure: 3 g anorectally every 12 hours for 7 days in the study

results.systemic_signals: Sporadic signals below assay quantification limits

limitations: Healthy mucosa; small sample; not absence of absorption.
Exact new-article equivalence cannot be inferred from concentrations alone.
Damaged mucosa increases relevance but postoperative wounds differ from chronic fissures.
Authors requested multiple-dose damaged-mucosa study; no universal no-systemic-exposure claim.

evidence_units.population: Chronic fissure refractory to conservative care
evidence_units.design: Reported randomized single-blind; allocation/concealment details limited
limitations: Ten post-allocation exclusions: five surgery for poor response, five nonadherence/lost.
Different strength; no direct combination comparison.
Table prints 42(60%); narrative and arithmetic support 42/60=70%.
Primary endpoint negative; day7 reporting does not establish p<0.05.
Adds nifedipine to lidocaine in a different surgical indication; does not test lidocaine addition.
Bracco sponsorship and employees; not independent of core Italian research lineage.

evidence_units.population: Chronic fissure defined as >4 weeks with clinical signs
limitations: Ten lost after allocation; complete-case analysis, unblinded.
Coadministration is not verified identical fixed-combination article.
Stool/diet/bath support in all groups; no usable recurrence estimate extracted.

evidence_units.design: Randomized, outcome assessors blinded; participants not blinded
limitations: Acute population; three diltiazem nonadherent withdrawals.
Reported recurrence percentages do not align cleanly with healing denominators; pain-duration units conflict.
Self-reported dizziness/flushing/hypotension exist; do not claim universally no systemic effects.

evidence_units.population: Mixed acute, chronic and acute-on-chronic fissure
limitations: Different lidocaine strength from 1.5% article; chronic-only effect unverified.
No vehicle/nifedipine-alone arm; similar results do not prove formal equivalence or superiority.
Short follow-up; no durable benefit established.

evidence_units.design: Retrospective uncontrolled complete-record series, 46 Indian sites
evidence_units.article: Nifedipine 0.3% plus lidocaine 1.5% cream; brand/vehicle equivalence unverified
limitations: Excludes incomplete records, recurrent fissures, hypertension, diabetes and several other conditions.
Supportive care and rescue acetaminophen allowed; no comparator or recurrence follow-up.
Two Samarth-employed authors; cannot infer causality or rare-event rates.
Acute setting, not chronic fixed-combination efficacy.
Counters the claim that hydrocortisone necessarily prevents all fissure healing; does not settle its role in the 2002 comparator.

facts: CCBs or nitrates for typical hypertonic chronic fissure: 1B.
Favorable reimbursement opinion but low clinical benefit and no added clinical value (ASMR V).
HAS questions comparator and unproven lidocaine contribution; pain/recurrence evidence inadequate.

nontrial_records.record_type: Approved label and apparent same-cohort clinical summary
facts: Adults with chronic primary fissure unresponsive to stool softeners and topical anesthetics.
P001/98: n110, day21, 52/55 versus9/55 complete/almost-complete healing.
Boxed methemoglobinemia warning and cardiovascular contraindications; no universal safety claim.
nontrial_records.deduplication: Treat P001/98 and EU02 as one apparent lineage pending full dossier reconciliation, not an extra efficacy trial.

commercial_unit_check.source_locator: Recommended dose and patient information; 30 g tube
commercial_unit_check.observed_label: Approximately 2.5–3 g twice daily for three weeks.
commercial_unit_check.status: Arithmetic from the Canadian labeled regimen, not observed purchasing or a treatment recommendation.
commercial_unit_check.economic_limit: Actual dispensing, adherence and repeat purchases are not measured. Higher course cost can reduce uptake. This quantity cannot be transferred to the Fizurex wipe or differently dosed compounded articles.
